def: A proton pump inhibitor in a dual delayed-release capsule that blocks the gastric H+/K+ ATPase, reducing acid for GERD and erosive esophagitis.
A proton pump inhibitor that irreversibly blocks the parietal cell H+/K+ ATPase, used for GERD and peptic ulcers. Long-term use risks hypomagnesemia, fractures and C. difficile.
A poorly absorbed magnesium salt used as an antacid and osmotic laxative. Excess magnesium can cause diarrhea and, in kidney disease, hypermagnesemia.
A bulk-forming fiber laxative that absorbs water in the gut to soften and enlarge stool.
A stimulant laxative that increases colonic motility and secretion by acting on the enteric nerves of the bowel wall.
A substance that speeds bowel evacuation, such as stimulant, osmotic or bulk laxatives.
A nucleoside analog antiviral that inhibits hepatitis B DNA polymerase. Associated with myopathy and peripheral neuropathy.
A drug or agent that induces termination of pregnancy, such as misoprostol or mifepristone.
Proteins that activate G proteins by prompting release of GDP so GTP can bind, switching the G protein on.
A cGMP-dependent kinase activated by nitric oxide signaling that phosphorylates targets to relax vascular smooth muscle.
A cytosolic enzyme activated by nitric oxide that converts GTP to cGMP, causing smooth muscle relaxation.
Membrane guanylyl cyclase receptor that raises cGMP when bound by ANP, promoting sodium excretion and vasodilation.
A kinase activated when calcium-bound calmodulin binds it, phosphorylating proteins in signaling, memory and muscle.
A neurotrophin that supports survival and growth of sympathetic and sensory neurons via the TrkA receptor.
Intracellular receptors that bind steroid hormones, then enter the nucleus and act as transcription factors.
Neural extension of the hypothalamus that stores and releases oxytocin and ADH from axons of hypothalamic neurons.
A fragment of POMC that gives rise to beta-endorphin; co-secreted with ACTH.
A hypothalamic hormone that stimulates somatotrophs of the anterior pituitary to release growth hormone.
A benign pituitary tumor that makes excess growth hormone, causing gigantism in children and acromegaly in adults.
Thyroglobulin intermediate with two iodines on tyrosine; two combine to form T4.
Thyroglobulin intermediate with one iodine; combines with DIT to form T3.
Gq-coupled receptor on pituitary thyrotrophs and lactotrophs that responds to TRH by releasing TSH and prolactin.
Mineralocorticoid precursor of corticosterone and aldosterone. Excess in 11-beta or 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypertension.
Melanocortin 2 receptor on adrenocortical cells that binds ACTH to stimulate cortisol synthesis.
Linear skin scars from dermal stretching and tearing, seen in pregnancy, rapid weight gain and Cushing syndrome.
Plasma protein that binds cortisol, raised by estrogen; also called transcortin.
Hormone from PP cells of the islets that inhibits pancreatic secretion and gallbladder contraction.
Channels in pancreatic beta cells that close when ATP rises, depolarizing the cell and triggering insulin release. Sulfonylureas close them.
Fat stored within the abdominal cavity around organs, strongly linked to insulin resistance and cardiovascular disease.
A first-generation bisphosphonate that inhibits osteoclast bone resorption, used for Paget disease.
Nuclear receptor bound by calcitriol, regulating genes for calcium absorption.
Inactive vitamin D metabolite made by 24-hydroxylase to inactivate calcitriol.
Calcium-binding protein in intestinal epithelium and kidney, induced by vitamin D, that carries calcium across cells.
Large eosinophilic mitochondria-rich cells in the parathyroid gland. Hurthle cells in thyroid are similar.
Calcium deposits within kidney parenchyma, seen in hypercalcemia, hyperparathyroidism and renal tubular acidosis.
Islet cells that secrete glucagon to raise blood glucose; located at the islet periphery.
Lipid signaling molecules made by the body, such as anandamide, that bind cannabinoid receptors.
Cytokine that drives monocyte differentiation to macrophages and osteoclast formation.
Intermediate-acting insulin complexed with protamine for delayed absorption, with peak at 4-12 hours.
Long-acting insulin analog that binds albumin to prolong action.
A first-generation sulfonylurea that stimulates insulin release by closing K-ATP channels.
G protein-coupled receptor on beta cells activated by GLP-1 agonists to increase insulin secretion.
Inflammation of the nose and pharynx; the common cold.
Drug class including metformin, which decreases hepatic glucose output via AMPK and improves insulin sensitivity.
Glycerol-3-phosphate with a phosphate, used in the glycerol phosphate shuttle in mitochondria.
A thiazolidinedione that activates PPAR-gamma to improve insulin sensitivity. Causes fluid retention and bladder cancer risk.
A thiazolidinedione PPAR-gamma agonist for type 2 diabetes; causes fluid retention and raised cardiac risk.
A nuclear receptor in adipose tissue that regulates fat cell differentiation and insulin sensitivity.
Sex steroids from testes and ovaries: testosterone, estrogen, progesterone.
A calcium supplement absorbed without acid.
The fallopian tube that carries eggs from ovary to uterus; the site of fertilization.
Cytokine receptor that signals through JAK2/STAT5 to stimulate lactation.
Testis-determining factor on the Y chromosome that triggers male gonadal development.
Sex-determining region on the Y chromosome initiating testis development. Its absence leads to female phenotype.
Congenital uterus duplication from incomplete fusion of Müllerian ducts, such as didelphys or bicornuate.
Ligament from uterine fundus through the inguinal canal to the labia majus; remnant of gubernaculum.
Cornea-specific keratin.
Transcription factor for skeletal muscle differentiation; a marker of rhabdomyosarcoma.
Determining the nucleotide order of DNA, for example by Sanger or next-generation methods.
Cells that can become any cell type of the three germ layers but not placenta.
The most common malignant ovarian epithelial tumor, with psammoma bodies; BRCA1/2 related.
Endometrial or ovarian cancer resembling endometrial glands, associated with unopposed estrogen.
Germ cell tumor of the ovary or testis with trophoblastic cells, producing hCG.
Ovarian fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion that resolve after tumor removal.
Formation of the placenta and its attachment to the uterus.
Disorders with small vessel clots, schistocytes, thrombocytopenia and organ damage, including TTP and HUS.
Red, velvety mucosal patch that is often precancerous, such as erythroplasia of Queyrat on the penis.
An enveloped RNA paramyxovirus causing parotitis, orchitis and meningitis.
Blood collection in a body cavity, such as the tunica vaginalis surrounding the testis.
Network of tubules in the testis that carry sperm from seminiferous tubules to efferent ducts.
Precancerous change of prostatic glands with atypical cells but intact basal layer.
Surgical removal of the whole breast without axillary dissection.
A radiolabeled compound used in imaging such as PET and nuclear scans.
Umbilical cord with only one artery, linked to congenital anomalies.
Giving estrogen to relieve menopausal symptoms; needs progestin if the uterus is present.
47,XYY syndrome: tall males, often normal fertility, with possible learning problems and behavior issues; due to paternal nondisjunction.
Presence of both ovarian and testicular tissue in an individual.
An oral bisphosphonate that inhibits osteoclasts, treating osteoporosis. Causes esophagitis; take upright with water.
TNF family protein on osteoblasts that binds RANK on osteoclast precursors, driving bone resorption; denosumab blocks it.
Receptor on osteoclast precursors activated by RANK ligand, promoting osteoclast formation.
syn: receptor activator of nuclear factor kappab

def: Enzyme converting arachidonic acid to leukotrienes; zileuton inhibits it.
Phospholipid in mature fetal lung surfactant; its presence indicates lung maturity.
Deficient testosterone or sperm production from testicular or pituitary failure; formerly eunuchism.
The initiating amino acid in bacterial and mitochondrial protein synthesis.
DNA sequence where replication starts, AT-rich; bacteria have one, eukaryotes many.
Enzyme that degrades RNA.
Enzyme that removes RNA primer flaps in lagging strand synthesis.
Enzyme that degrades RNA in RNA-DNA hybrids, removing primers and acting in retroviral replication.
Undifferentiated cells in tissues that renew and replace cells, e.g., hematopoietic stem cells.
Rapid premature aging from LMNA mutation producing abnormal lamin A (progerin).
Single nucleotide substitution changing an amino acid, such as sickle cell Glu6Val.
Bacterial protein binding cAMP to activate lac operon transcription when glucose is low.
Enzyme sealing nicks between DNA fragments (Okazaki) by forming a phosphodiester bond; uses ATP or NAD+.
Transcription factor subunit (TFIID) that binds the TATA box to start RNA polymerase II transcription.
DNA-binding motif of two alpha helices with leucine residues that dimerize.
Small rRNA of the large ribosomal subunit, transcribed by RNA polymerase III.
Enzyme that transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and some small RNAs.
Bile salt conjugated with taurine; emulsifies fat in digestion.
Death cap mushroom toxin that inhibits RNA polymerase II, causing liver failure.
RNA in the nucleus, such as hnRNA and snRNA.
Short RNA that regulates gene expression without coding for protein, e.g., miRNA, siRNA.
Modified uridine in tRNA and rRNA that stabilizes RNA structure.
Methionine-carrying tRNA that begins translation at AUG start codon.
RNA element that recruits ribosomes to start translation without a 5' cap, used by viruses.
Proteins that help assemble the ribosome at the start codon to begin translation.
Proteins (eIFs) that help assemble the 40S ribosome and initiator tRNA on mRNA.
Monomeric GTP-binding proteins like Ras and Rho that act as molecular switches.
Chaperones induced by stress that assist protein folding and prevent aggregation.
Rough endoplasmic reticulum clusters in neuronal cell bodies and dendrites, producing proteins. They disperse with axon injury (chromatolysis).
ER without ribosomes that synthesizes steroids and lipids and detoxifies drugs.
Small protein that tags other proteins for degradation by the proteasome.
Intermediate filament proteins forming the nuclear lamina that supports the nuclear envelope.
Paired cylinders of microtubules in the centrosome that organize the mitotic spindle.
Motor protein in cilia and flagella causing bending; defects cause primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener).
Mirror-image arrangement of internal organs, often in Kartagener syndrome.
Autoimmune inflammation of cartilage causing ear and nose collapse.
Type IV collagen (COL3A1) defect causing fragile blood vessels and organs prone to rupture.
Type III collagen fibers forming delicate supportive meshwork in liver, spleen and bone marrow.
Formation of dentin by odontoblasts.
Inherited defect of dentin causing opalescent teeth, linked to osteogenesis imperfecta.
Fibrillin-containing fibers that provide a scaffold for elastin, defective in Marfan syndrome.
Cross-link amino acid in elastin formed from lysine residues.
Short labeled DNA strands that hybridize to complementary sequences.
Proteins that bind DNA to regulate transcription, replication and repair.
Technique detecting DNA-binding proteins by probing a protein blot with labeled DNA.
Heat-stable DNA polymerase from Thermus aquaticus used in PCR.
Compound that absorbs light and emits it at a longer wavelength, used to label cells and DNA.
Tendency of nearby loci on a chromosome to be inherited together; measured by LOD score.
The complete set of RNA transcripts in a cell at a given time.
Identifiable DNA variants used to track inheritance or disease genes.
Chip with DNA probes used to measure gene expression or detect variants.
Common single-base variation in the genome between individuals.
Solid-phase material with antibodies or antigens used in ELISA.
Study of chromosomes, e.g., karyotyping or FISH.
Four copies of one chromosome instead of two.
Reduction of gene expression without eliminating it, e.g., with siRNA.
Gene silencing in which small double-stranded RNA directs degradation of complementary mRNA.
Protein complex using siRNA or miRNA to cleave or block target mRNA.
Family tree showing inheritance of a trait.
X-linked dominant phosphate wasting from PHEX mutation, causing rickets; vitamin D resistant.
Maternal transmission of mitochondrial DNA mutations to all children, with heteroplasmy.
Mitochondrial encephalopathy, lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes, from maternally inherited mtDNA mutation.
Extra copy of a chromosome segment.
Proportion of a given allele in a population; basis for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
Process where heritable traits improving survival become more common.
Genes required for survival of cell or organism.
Long, thin spider-like fingers, characteristic of Marfan syndrome.
Displacement of the eye lens, upward in Marfan and downward in homocystinuria.
Cell uptake of extracellular fluid in small vesicles.
Accessory atrioventricular pathway in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome causing preexcitation.
Vein inflammation, often with thrombosis, causing a tender red cord.
Diseases caused by ion channel mutations, such as long QT syndrome, cystic fibrosis.
Granulomas with Anitschkow cells in rheumatic heart disease.
Aortic root dilation behind aortic valve cusps, where the coronary arteries originate.
Structural and electrical changes in the atrium that promote atrial fibrillation.
Implanted device delivering electrical pulses to pace the heart.
G protein-coupled receptor binding adenosine, slowing AV node conduction and dilating vessels.
Drugs like caffeine and theophylline that block adenosine receptors.
Venous clot crossing right-to-left through a patent foramen ovale to cause arterial stroke.
Dual blood supply to liver from portal vein (75%) and hepatic artery (25%).
Narrowing of brain arteries days after subarachnoid hemorrhage causing ischemia; treated with nimodipine.
Source of omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA that lowers triglycerides.
Polyunsaturated fats (EPA, DHA, ALA) that lower triglycerides and reduce inflammation.
Maximal air inhaled after normal expiration: tidal volume plus inspiratory reserve volume.
Measurement of volume changes; body plethysmography measures total lung capacity.
Volume exhaled in a set time during forced expiration, usually FEV1 in one second; reduced in obstructive disease.
Main surfactant phospholipid, reducing alveolar surface tension.
Pressure of a gas in equilibrium with its liquid; relevant to water vapor in alveolar air (47 mmHg).
Enzyme (cytochrome b5 reductase) converting methemoglobin back to hemoglobin.
Variant beta-globin common in Southeast Asia; causes mild anemia.
Globin chains (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) that combine in tetramers.
Red cell anion exchanger swapping chloride for bicarbonate; defects in spherocytosis.
Ratio of alveolar airflow to blood flow; normally about 0.8.
Heme in complex IV that transfers electrons to oxygen; inhibited by cyanide.
Lung infection by virus causing interstitial inflammation.
Fever over 38.3 C for more than 3 weeks without a diagnosis after workup.
Individual with two identical alleles at a locus.
Severe asthma attack unresponsive to standard bronchodilators.
Drugs such as pirfenidone and nintedanib that slow scarring in pulmonary fibrosis.
Small openings in peritoneal mesothelium that drain fluid into lymphatics.
Vein of the armpit, continuing from basilic vein, becoming subclavian at first rib.
Blood and air in pleural space, often from chest trauma.
Constitutive enzyme making prostaglandins that protect gastric mucosa and platelets; inhibited by aspirin.
Rare bleeding disorder with delayed bleeding and poor wound healing; normal PT and aPTT.
Activated transglutaminase that cross-links fibrin to stabilize clots.
Test of intrinsic and common coagulation pathways; prolonged by heparin or hemophilia.
Standardized prothrombin time ratio used to monitor warfarin.
Activated Hageman factor that starts the intrinsic pathway.
Activated factor XI that activates factor IX.
Activated factor VII that complexes with tissue factor to start the extrinsic pathway.
Platelet receptor binding von Willebrand factor for adhesion; deficient in Bernard-Soulier syndrome.
Enzyme activating plasminogen to plasmin to dissolve clots.
Activated factor IX that with VIIIa activates factor X.
Glycolytic enzyme making ATP by transferring phosphate from 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate to ADP.
Glycolytic enzyme moving phosphate from 3- to 2-position.
Four-carbon short chain fatty acid made by colonic bacteria and a fuel for colonocytes.
Three-carbon short-chain fatty acid producing propionyl-CoA, converted to succinyl-CoA.
Brush border enzyme splitting sucrose into glucose and fructose.
Three-carbon aldose sugar; intermediate in fructose metabolism.
TCA enzyme combining acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate to citrate.
TCA enzyme converting fumarate to malate; defects in hereditary leiomyomatosis.
Enzyme converting malate to oxaloacetate producing NADH in TCA cycle and malate shuttle.
